s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive respiratory distress and cyanosis in a young calf with severe cardiac anomalies
salient_findings: Grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur
Severe dilation of the right atrium and ventricle
key_facts: Grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur
Sinus tachycardia at 170 beats/min on electrocardiography
Severe dilation of the right atrium and ventricle on echocardiography
16 mm interatrial defect in the upper septum
6 mm muscular interventricular defect in the dorsal septum
Two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle
Bidirectional shunting at both septal defects

shortlist.label: Double Outlet Right Ventricle
shortlist.why_kept: Two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle

shortlist.label: Truncus Arteriosus
shortlist.why_kept: Single ventricle with two great vessels and septal defects

shortlist.label: Tetralogy of Fallot
shortlist.why_kept: Severe cyanosis, right ventricular dilation, and septal defects

shortlist.label: Transposition of the Great Arteries
shortlist.why_kept: Two great vessels arising from the right ventricle and bidirectional shunting

shortlist.label: Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Hypoplastic left ventricle and severely reduced mitral valve orifice

shortlist.label: Tricuspid Atresia
shortlist.why_kept: Severe tricuspid regurgitation and right ventricular dilation

shortlist.label: Pulmonary Atresia
shortlist.why_kept: Severe cyanosis and right ventricular dilation

shortlist.label: Ebstein's Anomaly
shortlist.why_kept: Severe tricuspid regurgitation and right ventricular dilation

raw.rationale: The presence of two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle, severe dilation of the right atrium and ventricle, and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Truncus Arteriosus
rejected.why: Only one great vessel arises from the heart in Truncus Arteriosus, which contradicts the finding of two great vessels in this case.

rejected.label: Tetralogy of Fallot
rejected.why: While Tetralogy of Fallot involves right ventricular outflow obstruction, the key feature of two great vessels arising from the right ventricle is not characteristic of this condition.

rejected.label: Transposition of the Great Arteries
rejected.why: This condition involves the aorta and pulmonary artery being reversed, but does not typically involve two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle.

rejected.label: Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome
rejected.why: Although there is a hypoplastic left ventricle, the primary issue in HLHS is the underdevelopment of the left heart, which does not explain the two great vessels arising from the right ventricle.

rejected.label: Tricuspid Atresia
rejected.why: Tricuspid atresia involves the absence of the tricuspid valve, which is not the primary finding in this case, where severe tricuspid regurgitation is noted instead.

rejected.label: Pulmonary Atresia
rejected.why: Pulmonary atresia involves the absence or closure of the pulmonary valve, which is not the primary issue in this case, where two great vessels arise from the right ventricle.

rejected.label: Ebstein's Anomaly
rejected.why: Ebstein's anomaly involves the abnormal formation of the tricuspid valve and right ventricle, but does not typically involve two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle.
